Implements
[programming spec 0002](../../specs/features/002-programming/specs/0002-automatic-collections.md).
Source and executable tests are canonical after implementation.

## Reconnaissance

Collections today are explicit, ordered membership rows that programming
blocks draw from. Spec 0001 already stores everything the required collection
types match on: series and franchise TMDB identities, genres, release dates,
and the owner's tags. Only tags lack a stable identity; they are a JSON array
of names on the correction row.

Exclusions, recommendation decisions, and tags get tables of their own, one file each. Membership rows keep their shape ([ADR 0006](../../adrs/0006-media-roots-and-collections.md)). |

Accepted ADRs: [ADR 0006](../../adrs/0006-media-roots-and-collections.md)
keeps collections as explicit ordered membership; automatic collections
materialize into the same rows, so no ADR change is needed.
[ADR 0003](../../adrs/0003-materialized-schedule-entries.md) protects the
airing entry; maintenance goes through `applyInputChange`, which already does.
[ADR 0009](../../adrs/0009-programming-blocks.md) keeps blocks consuming
collections, never criteria. [ADR 0010](../../adrs/0010-source-layout.md)
places the folders. [ADR 0013](../../adrs/0013-metadata-provider-calls-and-stored-key.md):
nothing here calls TMDB. Glossary terms used: **Media collection**,
**Automatic collection**, **Collection recommendation**, **Content metadata**,
**Correction**, **Catalog removal**, **Purge**, **Schedule revision**,
**Regeneration**, **Window dialog**, **Desktop program**.

### Design Decisions This Plan Makes

The spec leaves these open or to implementation; each ticket below follows
them. Change them here before the ticket lands, not inside it.

| Decision                        | Choice                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Criterion storage               | One JSON column holding `{ kind: "series", tmdbId }`, `{ kind: "franchise", tmdbId }`, `{ kind: "tag", tagId }`, or `{ kind: "genre", name }`. Its canonical string is the recommendation identity.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Series identity                 | The TMDB series ID. An item whose series the owner corrected to a name other than the provider's matches no series criterion until a later spec gives corrected series an identity, rather than guessing from the name. A correction naming the provider's own series, as track mapping (META-011) stores, keeps the identity, as does any correction while the provider's series name is unknown after expiry. |
| When maintenance runs           | One coalesced pass over every automatic collection, requested after any fact, tag, catalog, criterion, or exclusion commit and once at boot. It recomputes inside one `applyInputChange`, so it always reads committed facts.                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Revalidation                    | Falls out of the above: the pass reads mode, criterion, exclusions, and facts inside the same immediate transaction it writes in, so delayed work cannot undo a newer decision.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Default order                   | Series: season, then episode, then path. Movies: release date, then title, then path. Unknown values sort last. Spec 0003 may replace these later.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Recommendation threshold        | A series or franchise with at least two cataloged items. Tune later from real catalogs.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Duplicate files for one episode | Both appear in previews and membership, ordered by path. No merging in this scope.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Restoring dismissals            | **Show dismissed** in Discover lists dismissed recommendations with **Restore**. Deleting an accepted collection leaves its decision `accepted`, so the recommendation shows there as dismissed-by-deletion and can be restored.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Pause/resume                    | Not offered. Acceptance enables maintenance; conversion ends it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Directory-based suggestions     | Deferred. The spec allows them but no acceptance criterion needs them.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Missing members                 | Stay included, as the spec requires, but warn: each missing member is labelled as not airing until its file returns, and the card counts them. Applies to manual collections too, since their missing members cannot air either.                                                                                                                                                                                |

**Sequencing note**: COL-001 comes first. COL-002 needs COL-001. COL-003
needs COL-002. COL-004, COL-005, COL-006, COL-007, COL-009, and COL-010 each
need COL-003 and are otherwise independent. COL-008 needs COL-006. COL-011
needs COL-004 and COL-007. COL-012 needs nothing and blocks nothing.

### COL-001: Split Collections into Manual and Automatic tabs

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-13. Migration `014` adds the maintenance
mode, criterion, and diagnostics columns; the listing reports mode and member
count; Collections lands on Manual and Automatic card grids, and both
collection domains are regrouped into capability folders.

**Goal**: Collections opens on Manual and Automatic tabs, each a grid of
created collections, and every collection records whether it is maintained.

**Scope**:

- Migration `014` adds `maintenance_mode` (`manual` or `automatic`, default
  `manual`), a nullable `criterion`, and nullable maintenance diagnostics
  (`maintained_at`, `maintenance_error`, `maintenance_incomplete`) to
  `media_collections`.
- `GET /media-collections` returns mode and included member count.
- Regroup `apps/server/src/media-collections/` and `apps/web/src/collections/`
  into capability folders in this change.
- Two tabs with card grids. Cards show name and member count; opening a card
  opens the existing editor. Manual keeps **New collection…**. Automatic shows
  an empty state until COL-002 adds its actions.

**Out of scope**: Creating automatic collections; recommendations.

**Blocking dependencies**: None.

**Implementation notes**:

- Owner: backend-engineer for the migration and route; the web change is a
  thin UI slice.
- Every existing collection migrates as `manual`, so behavior is unchanged.

**Verification**:

- Migration test: existing collections read back `manual` with no criterion.
- Route test: the listing reports mode and member count.
- jsdom test: the Manual tab lists existing collections as cards and opens the
  editor; the Automatic tab shows its empty state.

**Docs impact**: Add **Manual collection** to `GLOSSARY.md`.

### COL-002: Create an automatic TV series collection on request

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-13. A pure series criterion orders matches
from the same effective facts the Media Library shows; the series listing,
preview, and automatic creation routes back a preview-and-confirm dialog,
automatic editors are read-only apart from rename and delete, and missing
members are counted and labelled in both modes.

**Goal**: The owner picks a series from the catalog, previews its episodes in
order, and creates an automatic collection that programming can use.

**Scope**:

- A pure criterion module in `media-collections/criteria/`: given effective
  facts for cataloged items, a series criterion returns ordered matching item
  IDs (the order in Design Decisions).
- `GET /media-collections/series` lists cataloged series with item counts.
- `POST /media-collections/previews` takes a criterion and returns ordered
  members; `POST /media-collections` accepts an optional criterion and creates
  an `automatic` collection with that membership.
- `PUT /media-collections/:id/items` answers `409 media_collection_automatic`
  for an automatic collection.
- **New automatic collection…** opens a window dialog: choose a series,
  preview, confirm. The editor shows the criterion and members read-only and
  still allows rename and delete.
- Missing-file warning, because automatic collections keep missing members:
  `GET /media-collections` also returns a missing member count, the card shows
  it, and the editor labels each missing member **Missing — won't air until
  the file returns** with text and an icon, not color alone. Manual and
  automatic collections show it alike.

**Out of scope**: Keeping it current after later changes (COL-003); other
criteria.

**Blocking dependencies**: COL-001.

**Implementation notes**:

- Owner: backend-engineer.
- Matching reads `effectiveMetadata` plus the series and franchise TMDB IDs;
  do not write a second facts query. Removed items never match; missing items
  do.
- The browser displays the server's preview; it never matches.

**Verification**:

- Unit tests for the criterion: episode order, unknown numbers last, removed
  items skipped, missing items kept, corrected series unmatched.
- Route tests: preview equals created membership; replacing members of an
  automatic collection answers `409`; a block can use the new collection.
- jsdom test: the dialog previews and creates; the card appears under
  Automatic.
- Route test: the listing counts missing members. jsdom test: a missing member
  shows the warning label and the card shows the missing count.

**Docs impact**: Add **Collection criterion** to `GLOSSARY.md`.

### COL-003: Keep automatic collections current

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-13. `CollectionMaintenance` coalesces
requests from scans and lookup retries, refreshes and expiry, corrections,
match decisions, track mappings, catalog removal, and boot into one pass
inside one `collection_maintained` input change that writes only changed
memberships; failures are logged and recorded, and cards and editors show
failed status with the last good time.

**Goal**: After catalog or metadata changes, automatic collections gain and
lose members without touching manual collections or the airing entry.

**Scope**:

- A `CollectionMaintenance` service in `media-collections/maintenance/` that
  coalesces requests into one pass: inside one `applyInputChange` with reason
  `collection_maintained`, it recomputes each automatic collection, writes
  membership only where it differs, and names only those collections' channels.
- The scan writer, lookup retry, refresh, corrections, match choice, track
  mapping, and catalog removal request a pass after they commit. A pass also
  runs at boot. `preClose` stops it with the other background services.
- Record `maintained_at` and `maintenance_error` per collection; cards show a
  failed or stale status.

**Out of scope**: Unavailable evidence (COL-005), exclusions (COL-006).

**Blocking dependencies**: COL-002.

**Implementation notes**:

- Owner: backend-engineer.
- Writers only call `request()`; they never compute membership or wait for
  the pass. A pass that fails logs and records the error; the next request
  converges from committed facts.
- Reuse `replaceCollectionMembers` for the write.

**Verification**:

- Acceptance test: a scan adds a new episode to the automatic series
  collection but not to a manual snapshot of the same episodes.
- A correction moving an episode's season reorders membership while the airing
  entry stays airing (`manual-clock.ts`).
- A no-op pass leaves every `scheduleRevision` unchanged.
- Race tests with `test-barrier.ts`: a pass held before commit does not
  recreate a collection deleted meanwhile or re-add a removed item.
- A failing pass records `maintenance_error` and is logged, not thrown.

**Docs impact**: None beyond this plan's Status block.

### COL-004: Create movie franchise collections

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-13. A franchise criterion keyed by the TMDB collection ID
orders by release, then title and path; `GET /media-collections/franchises`
lists franchises through the same grouping as series, and the dialog offers
series or franchise.

**Goal**: The owner creates an automatic collection for one movie franchise,
ordered by release.

**Scope**:

- A franchise criterion keyed by the TMDB collection ID, ordered by release.
- `GET /media-collections/franchises` lists cataloged franchises with counts.
- **New automatic collection…** offers series or franchise.

**Out of scope**: Recommendations (COL-011).

**Blocking dependencies**: COL-003.

**Implementation notes**: Owner: backend-engineer. A franchise and a series
stay separate criteria even when their items overlap.

**Verification**:

- Criterion tests: release order, partial dates, unknown dates last.
- Acceptance test: matching a new franchise movie adds it at its release
  position.

**Docs impact**: None beyond this plan's Status block.

### COL-005: Keep membership when evidence is unavailable

**Status**

Complete on 2026-10-13. One membership decision, shared by preview,
creation, and maintenance, keeps a member whose TMDB data expired, never adds
one, and records `maintenance_incomplete`, which cards and editors report;
picker counts leave expired items out the same way.

**Goal**: Expired or unavailable TMDB facts never empty a collection; the
card reports incomplete maintenance instead.

**Scope**:

- An item whose provider ref has `expired_at` set counts as unknown: a current
  member stays, a non-member is not added, and the collection records
  `maintenance_incomplete`.
- Catalog removal, exclusions, confirmed criterion changes, and tag changes
  still apply to unknown items.
- When a refresh restores facts, the next pass reconciles from them.

**Out of scope**: Retaining expired payloads; they stay dropped per spec 0001.

**Blocking dependencies**: COL-003.

**Implementation notes**: Owner: backend-engineer. Tag criteria need no
provider evidence, so they are never incomplete.

**Verification**:

- Maintenance tests with `metadata-refresh-fixtures.ts`: an expired member
  stays and marks the collection incomplete; a refresh clears the flag; a
  removed expired member still leaves.

**Docs impact**: None beyond this plan's Status block.

### COL-006: Exclude and restore items

**Goal**: The owner excludes an item from one automatic collection, and it
stays excluded through rescans and metadata changes until restored.

**Scope**:

- A `media_collection_exclusions` table keyed by collection and media item,
  cascading on collection delete; purge deletes rows for purged items.
- Routes to exclude and restore. Each requests a maintenance pass; a restore
  includes the item only if it currently matches.
- Editor: **Exclude from this collection**, **Show excluded**, an **Excluded**
  label with distinct styling that does not rely on color alone, whether the
  item still qualifies, and **Restore inclusion**.

**Out of scope**: Carrying exclusions across renamed or moved files.

**Blocking dependencies**: COL-003.

**Implementation notes**: Owner: backend-engineer. Exclusions are decisions,
never membership rows; programming never reads them.

**Verification**:

- Acceptance test: excluding two franchise movies keeps them out across a
  rescan and a correction while a new franchise movie still joins.
- An exclusion committed while a pass is held is not undone by that pass.
- Restoring an item that no longer matches leaves it out.
- jsdom test: excluded items show labelled and restorable.

**Docs impact**: Add **Collection exclusion** to `GLOSSARY.md`.

### COL-007: Convert an automatic collection to manual

**Goal**: The owner turns an automatic collection into a manual one that keeps
its members and order and is never maintained again.

**Scope**:

- `POST /media-collections/:id/conversion` sets `manual`, clears the
  criterion, exclusions, and diagnostics, and keeps membership rows.
- The editor offers **Convert to manual…** and points to it when the owner
  tries to add members or reorder.

**Out of scope**: Converting manual to automatic.

**Blocking dependencies**: COL-003.

**Implementation notes**: Owner: backend-engineer. Conversion changes no
membership, so it names no affected channels.

**Verification**:

- Route test: members and order are unchanged; a later scan adding a matching
  episode leaves the converted collection alone.
- A pass held across a conversion does not rewrite the converted collection.

**Docs impact**: None beyond this plan's Status block.

### COL-008: Change a collection's criterion with a preview

**Goal**: The owner changes an automatic collection's criterion after seeing
the resulting membership.

**Scope**:

- `PATCH /media-collections/:id` accepts a criterion; the editor previews it
  through `POST /media-collections/previews` before applying.
- Exclusions survive the change; renaming never changes the criterion.

**Out of scope**: Changing criterion kind across manual and automatic.

**Blocking dependencies**: COL-006.

**Implementation notes**: Owner: backend-engineer. The change commits inside
an input change with the new membership, so channels regenerate once.

**Verification**:

- Route tests: the preview equals the applied membership; an exclusion stays
  after the change; rename leaves the criterion alone.

**Docs impact**: None beyond this plan's Status block.

### COL-009: Give tags identities and create tag collections

**Goal**: The owner creates an automatic collection from one tag; tagging and
untagging items updates it.

**Scope**:

- Migration moves tags from the JSON column on `metadata_corrections` into a
  `tags` table and a `media_item_tags` join. The correction route still takes
  tag names and resolves them to IDs.
- A tag criterion keyed by tag ID. **New automatic collection…** offers tags in
  use; adding a tag never creates a collection.
- Tag changes request a maintenance pass.

**Out of scope**: Whole-series bulk tagging; renaming tags in the UI.

**Blocking dependencies**: COL-003.

**Implementation notes**:

- Owner: backend-engineer.
- Tag names compare case-insensitively when resolving to an ID, so
  `Christmas` and `christmas` are one tag.

**Verification**:

- Migration test: existing tags carry over to the same items.
- Acceptance test: a Christmas tag collection includes a tagged movie and one
  tagged episode but not its untagged siblings; untagging removes the item;
  a manual collection is untouched.

**Docs impact**: Add **Tag** to `GLOSSARY.md`; record the move in spec 0001's
data model only if that spec still serves an active purpose.

### COL-010: Create genre collections on request

**Goal**: The owner picks a standard genre, previews matching media, and
creates an automatic genre collection.

**Scope**:

- `GET /media-collections/genres` lists genres present in accepted facts.
- A genre criterion matching an exact accepted genre name.
- **New automatic collection…** offers genres with preview and confirm.

**Out of scope**: Recommending genres; descriptive themes (COL-012).

**Blocking dependencies**: COL-003.

**Implementation notes**: Owner: backend-engineer. Genre collections order by
release, like movie groups.

**Verification**:

- Route tests: a genre preview lists only items with that accepted genre; a
  collection named "Christmas" with an Action criterion includes no item merely
  for its name.

**Docs impact**: None beyond this plan's Status block.

### COL-011: Discover and accept recommendations

**Goal**: **Discover collections…** suggests series and franchise collections
with reasons and previews; the owner accepts each as automatic or as a manual
snapshot, or dismisses it.

**Scope**:

- A `collection_recommendation_decisions` table keyed by criterion identity,
  holding `accepted` or `dismissed`.
- `GET /media-collections/recommendations` computes series and franchise
  recommendations from the catalog (threshold in Design Decisions), each with
  reason, member count, preview, and whether a collection with that criterion
  already exists. Never genres or tags.
- Accept creates the collection and the decision in one immediate
  transaction; a second concurrent accept finds the decision and creates
  nothing. Dismiss records a decision; **Show dismissed** restores it.
- Discover opens inside the Collections program. Automatic is the primary
  action; **Save as manual collection** is the alternative.

**Out of scope**: Batch acceptance; directory-based suggestions.

**Blocking dependencies**: COL-004, COL-007.

**Implementation notes**: Owner: backend-engineer. Scans never create
collections; recommendations are computed on request only.

**Verification**:

- Route tests: two concurrent accepts create one collection; a dismissal
  survives a rescan; deleting an accepted collection does not bring it back;
  a manual snapshot does not gain a later episode.
- jsdom test: recommendations show reason and count, and neither grid shows
  one before acceptance.

**Docs impact**: Update the spec's `Status:` line when this ticket completes
the required delivery.

### COL-012: Spike descriptive theme collections

**Goal**: Decide whether a phrase such as "Pulpy Action Adventure" can become
an explainable automatic collection with modest effort.

**Scope**:

- Answer the spike questions in the spec: whether genres suffice or TMDB
  keywords would be needed, how The Mummy, Pirates of the Caribbean, and
  Indiana Jones compare with titles that should not qualify, and what lookup,
  persistence, refresh, and UI work keywords would add.
- Record evidence, a proposed rule, limits, an effort estimate, and a
  recommendation in `docs/knowledge_base/`.

**Out of scope**: Production code, keyword ingestion, or amending spec 0001.

**Blocking dependencies**: None. Blocks nothing; required delivery completes
without it.

**Implementation notes**: Owner: architect. Never pass TMDB data to a model.

**Verification**: The note answers each spike question and ends in implement
or defer.

**Docs impact**: One knowledge-base note; a later feature spec if deferred.
